scope: Independent source review of signaling, reconnect, credits, Disconnect retry, deadlines and CENTRAL-STOP-01.

review.result: The stop helper keeps refused Cancel and Scan Disable pending. D_CONTROL records acceptance. Accepted commands do not repeat.
review.detail: Pending original responses remain distinct from stop acceptance. Successful Command Status cannot complete a synchronous command. Failed responses set FAILED.

review.result: Each Disconnect entry uses the original cutoff. Repeated stop and direct start cannot erase an unresolved stop.
review.detail: A late successful connection retains its handle. At or after the cutoff, Disconnect is not submitted. A duplicate event cannot replace an active handle.

review.result: Command acceptance and status do not release the link. A matching successful Disconnection Complete restores the sole-link credits.
review.detail: Wrong handles and failed disconnection events do not release the retained handle. Credit arithmetic saturates before uint8_t conversion.

review.result: The actual service supplies fm1_ms before stop, receive and poll. TIMER5 owns this service and its clock update.
review.detail: The service drains old events before a fresh Reset. It continues the bounded stop when Bluetooth is off. A failed unresolved stop does not restart.

review.result: The four-entry signaling queue preserves identifiers and reply priority. ACL storage remains bounded at 64 bytes.
review.detail: Oversized signaling uses bounded storage and uint16_t drain counters. Lifecycle resets clear replies, fragments, running status and SysEx state.

review.result: The send callback retains mailbox acceptance semantics. The receive callback still queues complete MIDI messages for the main loop.
review.detail: No mapping or controller source changed in this stage. Notes, pad colours, controls and the normal MIDI path retain their existing source.

new_probe.reason: The saved stop cases duplicate the same successful connection handle. They do not combine a different successful handle with STOPPING or FAILED.
new_probe.coverage: Legacy and enhanced connection events, timer wrap, accepted and refused Disconnect, STOPPING and FAILED, a different handle, wrong disconnection, Bluetooth on and fresh startup.
new_probe.observation: The host retains handle 0x50 after a successful event for handle 0x51. Stop intent and the original cutoff survive. Accepted Disconnect does not repeat.
new_probe.completion: The matching successful disconnection permits a fresh Reset. A different handle and direct start cannot erase the unresolved stop.
new_probe.limits: The probe uses public startup helpers and the exact extracted production service. The mailbox, peer, clock and schedule are simulated.

reused_evidence.result: The four public stop controls fail on exact f080d1a5 and pass after repair. All five saved production service cases pass after repair.
reused_evidence.disposition: The source and scope match. These checks were not repeated. The test helper owns the complete evidence identity audit.

reused_evidence.result: The four realistic Cancel variants and all 12 saved event-order cases pass after repair.
reused_evidence.disposition: The source and scope match. These checks were not repeated.

reused_evidence.result: The 18 historical commands reproduce refused Cancel, refused Scan Disable and failed Scan Disable status on three exact revisions. Accepted controls pass.
reused_evidence.disposition: The failures establish the inherited CENTRAL-STOP-01 defect. They are historical broken-source controls, not current candidate failures.

reused_evidence.result: The four stale-service examples retain the old caller order. The old-caller mutation remains an expected negative control.
reused_evidence.disposition: These examples do not execute the repaired production service. They do not invalidate its matching passing service checks.

physical_limits: The owner reports that all SMC controls failed while light feedback operated. The owner states that the messages did not change.
The idle trace has CONNECTED, handles 114/115, five credits and continued polling. Zero idle counters do not prove input loss.
The rejected header contains no signaling command or identifier. Credit starvation reproduces discovery failure, which differs from the CONNECTED observation.
Recorded payload replay retains its simulated HCI framing, mailbox, clock and schedule. Three oversized ATT packets remain excluded. No payload resegmentation occurs.
The synthetic store and host probes do not test target interrupts or physical radio execution. This result does not establish the cause of the physical failure.
next_action: The task agent must combine both independent helper results before it selects the stage disposition.
